verbatim: The laptop's front edge is not aligned with the front edge of the table. Also, there is an extra piece of wood coming out of the top of the backrest of the chair.

localized_case_analysis.inspection_basis: Inspected the supplied full generated image and product reference, consulting the fixed quadrants for the laptop/table boundary and chair profile. The full image remains authoritative; overlapping crops are not independent evidence.
localized_case_analysis.change_from_previous_analysis: The new feedback redirects inspection from alleged TABLE construction to the CHAIR's upper backrest and separately challenges laptop/table alignment. That is a change in the propositions being evaluated, not evidence that the frozen labels previously meant these things.

issues.user_claim: The laptop's front edge is not aligned with the front edge of the table.
issues.member_ownership: The relevant laptop front is the palm-rest width edge extending from the low rounded near corner toward image right. The port-bearing left side is a depth edge. The comparison surface is the tabletop's upper front boundary, not the apron bottom or chair back.
evidence: The palm-rest front edge rises toward image right more steeply than the table's front boundary.
The hinge-side base-width boundary also rises rightward. The exposed table front and rear long boundaries form a shallower rightward-rising group.
The resulting tabletop margin in front of the laptop is not visually uniform.
counter_evidence: Corresponding parallel edges at different image positions need not have identical projected slopes or a uniform image-space separation.
The visible groups do not establish the conspicuous incompatible convergence and diagonal relationship present in the Cashmere conflict case.

The table's short boundaries are insufficiently exposed for a reliable independent depth-family comparison. Merely repeating the slope difference for two width boundaries would not resolve materiality.
issues.assessment: The feedback correctly identifies a visible projected-direction difference. I do not find sufficient evidence to upgrade that difference into a clear material product/table axis conflict. Exact physical alignment is also not established.
issues.consequence: No material alignment correction is established. The clear operating approach does not prove alignment, but neither does the slope difference independently prove consequential rotation.
issues.agreement_with_user: Partial agreement on the visible difference; disagreement with treating it as an established material placement failure.

issues.user_claim: There is an extra piece of wood coming out of the top of the backrest of the chair.
issues.member_ownership: The localized candidate I can identify is the short raised, lighter wooden profile near the image-right upper end of the curved chair backrest. It belongs to the chair silhouette, not the table apron. I cannot establish it as a separate extra member.
evidence: The chair has a broad curved wooden backrest with a visible narrow top surface and rounded ends.
Near its image-right crest, a small raised/light-toned portion is visible above the darker backrest face.
The descending wooden supports and seat are identifiable as chair parts; the backrest obscures portions of the upper support relationships.
counter_evidence: The candidate raised portion is compatible with the exposed thickness and rounded return of the curved backrest.
I do not resolve a distinct projecting branch, conspicuously malformed termination, duplicated member, or abrupt section inconsistency that distinguishes an extra piece from the backrest profile.
The visible upper profile does not establish that an upright has continued anomalously through or above the rail.
issues.assessment: I can localize the potentially disputed upper profile, but I cannot substantiate the claimed extra malformed piece from these pixels. This is not a finding that every chair joint is correct. A clearly unmotivated or malformed projection would qualify without requiring physical impossibility; that affirmative appearance inconsistency remains unresolved here.
issues.consequence: No material chair-construction correction is established. There is no independently demonstrated access, contact, scale, or chair-pose consequence to score elsewhere.
issues.agreement_with_user: The claimed malformed extra member is not visually substantiated at the material-failure threshold. I retain that disagreement rather than converting the clarification into proof.

historical_table_claim.status: Preserved as a separate unresolved historical disagreement.
historical_table_claim.assessment: The exposed deep front band and outer uprights still do not provide an affirmative table-construction defect. Cloth and the chair conceal some relationships. The new chair allegation neither proves nor retrospectively resolves the old TABLE label.

other_case_analysis.role: Human orientation anchor; construction is unlabeled.
evidence: The laptop's front and hinge-side width boundaries and the table's long boundaries have compatible rightward-rising directions in the full scene.
The exposed left tabletop return, top thickness, deeper apron, and broad upright remain distinguishable, without an exposed displacement or malformed termination.
The chair's curved upholstered upper edge is continuous. Its wooden support ends lie against the backrest below the upper outline rather than forming an unexplained projection above it.
other_case_analysis.transferable_mechanism: Preserve the distinction between a chair's ordinary support terminations and malformed extra members. The chair's lateral offset toward the sketchbook is not an alignment or access failure.
other_case_analysis.limit: The right table end and parts of the lower assembly are concealed or cropped. The construction finding is not human-certified negative ground truth.

other_case_analysis.role: Human material-orientation anchor; construction is unlabeled.
evidence: The table's extended front and rear long boundaries descend toward image right and spread apart rightward, while the laptop's front and hinge-side width boundaries rise rightward and narrow rightward.

Together, those internally coherent paired groups establish a conspicuous diagonal product/table relationship and a substantially widening front margin across the laptop. The finding does not rest on one differently sloped edge pair.
The chair's two rounded wooden support ends are visible against the backrest below its top rim. They are not unexplained pieces emerging above it.
The exposed table band and supporting members show no independent material construction inconsistency.
other_case_analysis.transferable_mechanism: Retain genuine rigid-axis conflict detection without turning ordinary chair members into construction defects. Good contact and accessible controls do not cancel the supported orientation finding.
other_case_analysis.limit: Table ends remain incompletely exposed. The readable width groups nevertheless support this finding; no complete-furniture requirement is introduced.

other_case_analysis.role: Model-selected stability control, not human gold.
evidence: The laptop base-width boundaries and the exposed table boundaries have compatible shallow directions.
The foreground chair has a broad curved top band with a continuous exposed upper profile. No separately readable malformed projection emerges above it.
The background chair and table belong to a separate seating group and should not be attributed to the foreground table's construction.
other_case_analysis.transferable_mechanism: A curved chair rim, its exposed thickness, and overlapping furniture are not affirmative extra-member defects. Cropped table ends do not justify manufacturing an alignment conflict.
other_case_analysis.limit: The lower chair and table construction are largely outside the image. This is a local visual stability reading, not a measured false-positive result.

other_case_analysis.role: Model-selected stability control, not human gold.
evidence: The printer's readable chassis-width boundaries and the table's long boundaries have compatible shallow rightward-rising directions.
The tabletop edge, deeper apron, and visible left upright form a readable local assembly; the apron is not an unexplained extra wooden member.
No associated chair is visible.
other_case_analysis.transferable_mechanism: Preserve correct ownership of top, apron, and upright. Do not infer malformation from depth, unfamiliar thickness, or cropped support structure.
other_case_analysis.limit: This control tests general member attribution and slope restraint, but it cannot test chair-top protrusion discrimination because no chair is shown.

other_case_analysis.role: Model-selected stability control, not human gold.
evidence: The printer's chassis-width direction is compatible with the desk's long boundaries.
The exposed wooden top, dark front frame, and left upright form a coherent local relationship.
The foreground upholstered chair has a continuous curved upper outline. Its dark arm structure is separate from the desk frame.
The shelving uprights at image left belong to another furniture assembly, not extra desk supports.
other_case_analysis.transferable_mechanism: Separate neighboring furniture and ordinary chair profiles before attributing an extra member. The adjacent chair's position does not establish a rigid-axis or operating-path conflict.
other_case_analysis.limit: Rear and right desk connections and the lower chair remain concealed. Wall association does not certify hidden fixings.

change_hypothesis.diagnosis: The clarification exposes a mismatch between the earlier disputed proposition and the user's current localization. Earlier discussion concentrated on table construction; the current construction allegation concerns the chair. That localization mismatch is established, but a newly detected material pixel defect is not.
change_hypothesis.transferable_policy_assessment: The existing prompts already require separate table/chair ownership, inspection of exposed contours and terminations, recognition of materially awkward construction without demanding impossibility, and restraint about projected-edge slope differences. This inspection does not demonstrate a missing policy that warrants another semantic revision.
change_hypothesis.decision: Do not author a cosmetic successor or loosen materiality to recover desired labels. Preserve the existing prompts and architectures pending affirmative evidence of a transferable failure mechanism.

chair_construction.label_change_vs_detection: A chair-positive finding would concern a different localized proposition from the frozen table-positive label, even though both use malformed_support_furniture. It must not be reported as retrospective recovery of the old table diagnosis.

prospective_criterion_expectations.scope: These are current visual assessments, not newly supplied human-negative labels or a global positive certification of the EliteBook scene. Both latest material-failure interpretations remain disputed.

remaining_limitations: The exact contour the user calls an extra piece is not unambiguously separable as an independent member. If a different feature is intended than the upper-right backrest profile discussed here, marking it on the full original would resolve localization, not automatically prove a defect.
The EliteBook image does not establish exact physical parallelism. Severity 0 here means no supported material conflict, not perfect alignment.
The chair assessment does not require a detached or impossible joint. A clearly malformed or unmotivated exposed projection would be sufficient, but I do not resolve one confidently in this view.
The old table-construction disagreement remains preserved and unresolved; the latest chair clarification does not silently replace its history.
The three stability controls are not independent human gold, and these inspections do not measure regression rate, robustness, or held-out accuracy.
Fixed quadrants remain consultation aids only. No new runtime, additional semantic samples, or evaluation results are claimed.

No changes are proposed to strict schemas, deterministic weights or scoring, the retired chair-pose code policy, P1 complementary primaries and requested-component-only verifiers, or P2 mutually blind specialists and final image reconciliation.
Transport/schema failures and incomplete predecessor expansion runs remain engineering and evaluation issues. They are not repaired by this analysis, and no promotion is claimed.
